name: AppRater

sources.title: Homepage — 'independent app archive since 2011', 11,074 apps listed; submission form lives at the /#submit anchor; leaderboard runs $5-per-bid promotion

requirements: App/software product on a named platform: Web, iOS, Android, Windows, MacOS, or Other
Every submission is human-reviewed before it appears in the archive

Form fields: app name, platform, app or store URL, 'what makes it useful?' description, optional comma-separated tags, optional image URL, your name, email, optional X username, website field (likely honeypot)
preparation: A substantive 'what makes it useful' paragraph — thin listings do get published but quality copy improves the entry
Tags, a direct image/logo URL, contact email, optional X handle (they tag you when the app is announced)
workflow: Open https://apprater.net/ and scroll to the 'Put your product in front of curious people' form (or use the /#submit anchor)
Fill app name, platform, URL, description, tags, image URL, name, email, X username
Leave the 'Website' field empty — it reads like a honeypot
Click 'Submit for review' and wait for editorial review
Optionally buy $5 bids later to climb the leaderboard (each payment = 1 bid on an approved app)
watchFor: Form is at the bottom of the homepage — /add, /submit, /submit-app all 404; /#submit is the only route
Leaderboard ranking is pay-to-bid ($5 per bid, newest bid wins ties) — organic listings rank low by default
'✦ Promoted' tags mark paid placements in the archive
Archive is a mixed bag (many thin or AI-generated descriptions); this is a low-bar index, not a curated showcase
countsAsLive: The app appears in the AppRater archive at apprater.net/a/<slug> and shows in browse/search with its description
unknowns: Review turnaround time and rejection rate
Whether the email provided gets a notification on approval
Link type on listings (dofollow vs nofollow)
Whether 'Website' is a honeypot field — left empty to be safe
